questions.question: What does `ProductionTokenizer.normalize` do before it splits text into chunks?
options: It removes all whitespace.
It converts every character to ASCII.
It NFKC-normalizes the text.
It replaces every word with a byte ID.
questions.explanation: The method calls `unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', text)`, which canonicalizes compatibility forms while retaining the normalized text.

questions.question: After `add_special_token('<|user|>')`, how should `encode` treat that exact marker?
options: As separate UTF-8 bytes and then ordinary BPE merges.
As whitespace that is dropped before encoding.
As an unknown word that is replaced by padding.
As one atomic token ID registered by the handler.
questions.explanation: `split_with_specials` marks registered markers as special, and `encode` emits their single registered ID instead of tokenizing their characters.

questions.question: Why does the production tokenizer count and apply BPE pairs within each pre-tokenized chunk?
options: It keeps merges inside each regex chunk.
It makes every chunk have the same number of tokens.
It guarantees that every merge is a Unicode character.
It removes the need for a vocabulary.
questions.explanation: The training loop builds byte sequences for each regex chunk separately, so adjacent bytes from different chunks are never presented as a merge pair.

questions.question: What problem does the byte-level fallback solve for a new Unicode character?
options: It sorts the character into the most common word.
It represents unseen characters as UTF-8 bytes.
It changes the character into an ASCII space.
It skips the character so the sequence length stays fixed.
questions.explanation: The base vocabulary contains all 256 byte values, so any UTF-8 string can be represented even when no larger merge was learned.

questions.question: A tokenizer has only its 256 byte entries and then calls `add_special_token('<s>')`. Which ID is the first available ID?
options: 257, after skipping the first free ID
questions.explanation: `next_id` starts at 256 after the byte vocabulary, so the first added special token receives 256.

questions.question: After registering `<|assistant|>` and encoding it as one special token, what does `get_token_bytes` return for that ID?
options: The UTF-8 bytes for the previous ordinary word.
An empty byte string because specials are discarded.
The integer ID encoded as decimal text.
The marker's stored UTF-8 bytes.
questions.explanation: `add_special_token` stores the marker's UTF-8 bytes in `vocab`, so `get_token_bytes` returns those bytes for the registered ID.
